_note: One-sentence summaries shown under the daf title above the outline (AnyDafWeb). DRAFTS for the author's review, 2026-10-16: chagigah_6 and bava_metzia_10 are the author's own examples; the rest were written by hand from each outline's sections (no API). In production these will come from the outline pass.
chagigah_6: Discussion of: Beit Shammai's ruling that a minor is obligated if he can be carried on his father's shoulders from Jerusalem to the Temple; the nature of chinukh; the Beit Hillel / Beit Shammai debate about the minimum cost of the olat re'iyah and the shalmei chagigah; the nature of the olah brought at Mt. Sinai; and whether re'iyah has no minimum and/or no maximum.
bava_metzia_10: Discussion of: the Amoraic debate whether picking up a lost object for someone else acquires it for that person; Reish Lakish's ruling that a person's four amot acquire on his behalf, and how this might not apply in every location (the public domain, another's property); Reish Lakish and R. Yochanan's debate about how a minor girl's property acquires on her behalf (is it like her hand or her agent?); and how a courtyard owned by a thief can be part of an act of theft (if one cannot make an agent for a sinful act).
bava_metzia_11: Discussion of: the two reasons a chatzer may steal for its owner despite ein shaliach le'dvar aveirah (the agent is not bound, or the agent could refuse); the proof from a get that a chatzer works as a woman's hand, and three ways to recast the dispute of R. Yannai and Abba Kohen Bardela; the Mishnah's ruling that a field acquires a found animal that cannot escape; Shmuel's requirement that the owner stand beside his field, and its source in the forgotten sheaf; and Rabban Gamliel's tithes given from a ship (chatzer, kinyan agav or da'at acheret?).
bava_metzia_2: Discussion of: the Mishnah of two holding a garment or an animal, each swearing he owns no less than half, and dividing it; why the Mishnah needs both "I found it" and "all of it is mine" (does seeing a found item acquire it?); and whether the Mishnah follows Ben Nannas, who rejects an oath that must be false, or Sumakhos, who divides uncertain property without an oath.
bava_metzia_3: Discussion of: R. Yochanan's view that the garment oath is a rabbinic takkanah against grabbing; when disputed property is divided and when it is set aside until Elijah comes (the Rabbis and R. Yosi, the storekeeper and the laborer); and R. Chiya's ruling that witnesses to part of a claim obligate an oath, derived by kal va'chomer from modeh be'miktzat and tested against fines, offerings and hazamah.
bava_metzia_4: Discussion of: whether one who admits part of a debt and says heilakh ("here it is") is a modeh be'miktzat who must swear or a kofer ha'kol who is exempt (R. Chiya vs. Rav Sheshet); and the baraita of a note with no amount written, used to challenge each side in turn.
bava_metzia_5: Discussion of: Rav Sheshet's view of heilakh tested against the Mishnah of vessels and land; Rami bar Chama's four bailees, who swear only when they deny part of the claim; whether witnesses to part of a claim obligate an oath (R. Chiya vs. the father of R. Aptoriki); the shepherd who denied, and who swears when a robber cannot; and Rav Huna's wording of the garment oath, "I have a share in it."
bava_metzia_6: Discussion of: why two holding a garment must swear, and whether a person suspected about money is suspected about oaths (migo de'chashid amamona); R. Zeira's question whether seizing the garment in front of the court counts; and whether consecrating a disputed item counts as seizing it (the disputed bathhouse and the safek bechor).
bava_metzia_7: Discussion of: which doubtful animals are tithed; the rule that what one cannot recover in court one cannot consecrate (the disputed bathhouse); Rav Tachlifa's baraita that each holder of a garment keeps what is in his hand, and kinyan sudar; two holding a promissory note (ratify it, divide it, or keep it from both?); whether it matters which part of the note each holds (tofes or toref); and whether "they divide" means cutting the item.
bava_metzia_8: Discussion of: Rami bar Chama's rule that lifting a found item for someone else acquires it for him, and Rava's limit to migo; which clause of the Mishnah is Rami bar Chama's source; and whether riding an animal (rakhuv) or leading it (manhig) acquires it, from Shmuel's forgotten rulings and the laws of kilayim.
bava_metzia_9: Discussion of: whether riding (rokhev) acquires an animal, tested against three baraitot; whether pulling an animal acquires the vessels on it, and Rava's rule that a moving chatzer (chatzer mehalekhet) acquires nothing; the Mishnah of a rider who asks a pedestrian to hand him a found item; and acquiring for another, through the pe'ah dispute and the count of migos.
bava_batra_84: Discussion of: Rav Chisda's ruling that only the exploited party (ona'ah) may cancel a sale when prices later shift; Rav Pappa's inference from shechamtit that the sun is red; whether wine and vinegar count as one type; the Mishnah's rules for acquiring produce by meshikhah and flax by hagbahah; whether produce measured into a simta (alleyway) is acquired; and the start of Rav and Shmuel's statement on where a person's vessels acquire.
bekhorot_10: Discussion of: why R. Shimon counts meat cooked in milk as food (it is permitted in benefit); whether the firstborn donkey (peter chamor) is forbidden once its neck is broken (arifah), and the principle issuro zehu machshavto; and betrothing a woman with a peter chamor.
bekhorot_11: Discussion of: how much the lamb that redeems a firstborn donkey must be worth (a shekel, any value, or a ragya); Reish Lakish's ruling that one may redeem with the donkey's value; who keeps a donkey that a stranger redeemed; cases where one must redeem or separate but may keep the gift; and the redemption lamb that died.
bekhorot_12: Discussion of: the Mishnah's list of animals unfit to redeem a peter chamor, and R. Eliezer's view of the hybrid; ben Bag Bag's gezeirah shavah from the Pesach, limited by the doubled "you shall redeem"; and borderline cases: a ben pekua, a lamb that looks like another species, and redeemed pesulei ha'mukdashin.
bekhorot_13: Discussion of: an animal bought with Shevi'it produce (redeeming a donkey with it, its own bekhorah, and challah); redeeming the donkey in the owner's presence, since every kohen is suspect; whether designating the lamb completes the redemption; whether a peter chamor is redeemed at once or after thirty days; which mitzvah comes first (redemption before arifah, yi'ud, yibum); a gentile's share exempting an animal from bekhorah; and whether money (kesef) or pulling (meshikhah) acquires from a gentile.
bekhorot_14: Discussion of: whether a Jew acquires from a gentile with money or with meshikhah, read four ways in the baraita of an idol found among scrap metal; the Mishnah contrasting an animal blemished before it was consecrated (kedushat damim) with one consecrated first (kedushat ha'guf); and the laws of the first case: bekhor, shearing, offspring and slaughter outside.
bekhorot_15: Discussion of: why an animal blemished before it was consecrated makes no temurah, yet may be redeemed even after it dies; what sanctity still governs an animal consecrated and then blemished (firstborn, priestly gifts, shearing, milk, offspring); and a baraita setting the two categories side by side.
bekhorot_16: Discussion of: the baraita's summary rules for redeemed consecrated animals; whether their offspring may be redeemed; Rav Huna's reading that one who slaughters them outside is liable for a minor eye blemish; why a temurah made after redemption must die; the Mishnah of tzon barzel (a gentile's flock taken at a guaranteed value) and of a ewe that bears a goat-like young; and who owns a tzon barzel flock (the firstborn exemption vs. ribbit).
bekhorot_17: Discussion of: how many generations of a tzon barzel flock are exempt (Rav Huna vs. Rav Yehuda); what R. Meir obligates in a nidmeh (an animal that looks like another species); the requirement of animals and materials "unchanged since creation" for the New Moon goat, wool and wine; twin males at a first birth; and whether the Rabbis allow exact measurement in human hands (tzamtzum).
bekhorot_18: Discussion of: the Rabbis' ruling of one jointly brought eglah arufah, showing that even human measurement can't be exact; two males born to one ewe (which lamb the priest takes, priestly gifts from the kept lamb, and when one dies); the Mishnah of two ewes; and why all three of R. Akiva's cases are needed.
bekhorot_19: Discussion of: the Mishnah of an animal born through the side (yotzei dofen) and the one born after it; and whether a bekhor le'davar echad (a firstborn in only one respect) counts as a firstborn.
berakhot_31b: Discussion of: the laws of prayer and of rebuke learned from Hannah's prayer and Eli's response; the wording of Hannah's vow (Tzeva'ot, im ra'o tireh, "Your maidservant" three times, zera anashim); Hannah bringing Samuel to Eli, and Samuel ruling before his teacher; al libah and a tangent on fasting on Shabbat; and Hannah and Elijah speaking boldly toward Heaven.
gittin_18: Discussion of: whether the date in a get helps when it is delivered long after it was written; whether a divorcee's three-month wait counts from the writing or from the delivery (Rav vs. Shmuel); when a ketubah becomes a debt cancelled by Shemittah; a ketubah or get written by day and signed at night; and ten men told to write a get (are two of them witnesses and the rest signing by stipulation?).
hullin_88: Discussion of: when blood plasma counts as blood, and why a corpse's liquids are pure; how much spurted blood and blood on the knife must be covered; which materials may be used for kisui ha'dam and what counts as "earth" (afar); and Rava on Abraham's words that earned his descendants mitzvot.
kiddushin_2: Discussion of: the opening Mishnah of the three ways a woman is betrothed (kesef, shtar, bi'ah) and the two ways she goes free; why the Mishnah says "a woman is acquired" rather than "a man betroths"; and the wording bi-shalosh derachim (why shalosh, and why "ways").
kiddushin_3: Discussion of: why the Mishnah speaks of "ways" (derakhim) rather than "matters"; what the Mishnah's numbers exclude (chuppah, chalipin, chalitzah); and the source of betrothal by money, and why a daughter's betrothal money goes to her father.
kiddushin_4: Discussion of: why a na'arah's betrothal money goes to her father (ein kesef); two laws learned from ein kesef and its extra yod; why betrothal money and earnings each need their own verse; why the amah ivriyah is freed twice, at youth and at adulthood; and ki yikach as a second source for kiddushei kesef.
kiddushin_5: Discussion of: why betrothal by intercourse needs the verse u've'alah and can't be derived from the yevamah; betrothal by document (shtar), and why divorce by money is excluded; why no mode can be derived from the other two; Rav Huna's argument that chuppah betroths; who must give the money and who must say the words; and Shmuel's rule that the formula must change her status, not his.
kiddushin_6: Discussion of: which declarations effect kiddushin, from clear formulas to unusual phrases; silent kiddushin while still on the topic (R. Yosei vs. R. Yehuda); the wording of divorce and manumission; betrothal by means of a loan; and money given on condition that it be returned (matanah al menat le'hachzir).
kiddushin_7: Discussion of: betrothal money that passes through a third party (a guarantor, a Canaanite slave, an adam chashuv); betrothing half a woman, and why it doesn't spread through her like hekdesh; unresolved questions of dividing a perutah, the woman, or the transaction; and whether silk used for betrothal must be appraised.
kiddushin_8: Discussion of: whether an item given as money needs a set value (the priest's own valuation at pidyon ha'ben); R. Elazar's ruling when a hundred is promised and one dinar given; betrothing with collateral (mashkon); and the woman's response to the money.
kiddushin_9: Discussion of: replies that do not accept kiddushin ("give it to a poor person," "give, give"); closing rulings on silk, the promised hundred and collateral; betrothal by document (who writes it, for whom, and with whose consent); and the source of kiddushei bi'ah.
kiddushin_10: Discussion of: what each sage learns from u'be'alah and be'ulat ba'al about kiddushei bi'ah; whether bi'ah acquires at its beginning or its end; and whether bi'ah creates full marriage (nisu'in) at once or only erusin.
kiddushin_11: Discussion of: three explanations of why Beit Shammai require a dinar for betrothal with money: a woman's dignity, Torah money as kesef Tzuri, and the amah ivriyah who deducts.
kiddushin_12: Discussion of: Reish Lakish's derivation of Beit Shammai's dinar from the amah ivriyah, and Rava's reason (so that women are not treated as hefker); whether Beit Hillel's perutah is any small amount or a fixed value; Shmuel's concern that even an item worth less than a perutah might betroth (safek kiddushin); and the acts for which Rav would flog (improper betrothal, undermining a divorce, contempt for the Sages).
niddah_60: Discussion of: the Mishnah of a ketem (stain) on a garment lent to a gentile or a niddah, or shared by several women; to whom a woman may attribute a ketem; R. Nechemia's rule that what cannot become impure takes no ketem; and three women in one bed with blood found under one of them.
sanhedrin_6b: Discussion of: the Tosefta's four positions on whether a judge may steer litigants toward compromise (bitzua); teachings on "You shall not be afraid before any man" (when a judge may decline a case, a student's duty to speak up, witnesses and judges); and what counts as the gmar din, and whether the halakha follows R. Yehoshua ben Korcha that bitzua is a mitzvah.
shabbat_21: Discussion of: what tar and wax are; which wicks and oils the Mishnah forbids for the Shabbat lamp, and why; adding good oil to unfit oil; unfit wicks and oils in the Temple and for Hanukkah; how many Hanukkah lights to kindle and where to place them; what Hanukkah is, and the miracle of the cruse of oil; and the Hanukkah lamp that set fire to a passing camel's flax.
shabbat_38: Discussion of: food left on the stove from Friday that cooked on Shabbat; returning a pot to the stove on Shabbat (chazarah), and what ends that right; the Mishnah's rules for an oven (tanur) and a kupach; and heating without fire: an egg roasted by indirect heat and the Tiberias hot-spring pipe.
yevamot_33: Discussion of: R. Chiyya and bar Kappara's opposite reports of Rebbi's rulings, and whether one prohibition can take effect on another; which Temple service a zar could perform on Shabbat in violation of several prohibitions; and the Mishnah of two couples whose brides were switched at the wedding canopy.
